solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, directions as headed); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: More than one stocky American tosses caber — that's out of order

indicators.note: the two parts are taken in the opposite order to the clue's, so the phrase is read back to front as a whole

parts.note: a caber is a tree trunk, a length of wood tossed at Highland games
to toss is to chuck

explanation.surface: A Highland games scene in which some burly American flings the caber about against the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tosses caber' read as CHUCKS WOOD is put 'out of order', the two words swapped. A caber is the heavy pole thrown at Scottish Highland games.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodchuck, or groundhog, is a thickset North American marmot, so several of them are stocky American animals.

clue.text: Promise daughter fight is over

indicators.note: turned over in a down clue, the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: a row is a quarrel or fight

explanation.surface: A girl swears the quarrel has finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving your word means making a pledge, so word and promise are synonyms.

clue.text: Boer War regulars embracing cold killer

indicators.note: the picked letters hug the other letter inside them
regular letters are every other one, here the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: Professional soldiers of the Boer War holding a cold-blooded murderer.
explanation.definitionFit: The orca is the killer whale, so 'killer' is a shortened name for it.

clue.text: Explorer's contacts arranged to tour island after school group

indicators.note: touring goes all round, so the shuffled letters surround the others
arranged letters are set out in a new order
the island's letter comes after the school group's

parts.note: the PTA is the Parent-Teacher Association

explanation.surface: A traveller's acquaintances are organised into an island trip after a school party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Explorer's' reads as 'the explorer is'. The rearranged letters split around the school group and island, which sit inside them as 'to tour' requires; the PTA is a British school's parents' association.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Falcon Scott led the British polar expedition that reached the South Pole in 1912.

clue.text: Nice one — collecting rent for Green?

indicators.note: the outer word gathers the inner one into itself

parts.note: in Nice, a French city, 'one' is une
a rent is a tear or rip

explanation.surface: Praise for someone who has just collected the rent on behalf of an environmentalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is the French city, so the word for one is French.
explanation.definitionFit: Green fruit is not yet ripe, so green here means immature.

clue.text: Turner maybe eager to embrace half of sportsmen

indicators.note: the outer word holds the inner one within it

parts.note: keen means eager

indicators.note: only the first half of the word is used

parts.note: athletes are sportsmen

explanation.surface: A painter keen to hug some of the athletes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' suggests the painter J M W Turner; here it is the actress.
explanation.definitionFit: Kathleen Turner is an American actress, so Turner is an example given by surname.

clue.text: Man of the cloth defrocked, and then again

indicators.note: defrocking strips the front, done here twice, so the first letter is removed and then the next first letter too

parts.note: a man of the cloth is a clergyman, a cleric

explanation.surface: A priest is struck off, and then it happens to him all over again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man of the cloth' looks like the definition, but 'Man' alone defines; 'of the cloth' gives CLERIC, which loses its first letter twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric is a man's first name, a crossword-style definition by example.

clue.text: Release north Parisian who interrupts enjoyment

indicators.note: breaking into something puts these letters inside it

parts.note: relish is keen enjoyment
a Parisian, speaking French, says qui for who

explanation.surface: A Frenchman from the north spoils the fun and is let go.
explanation.definitionFit: To relinquish something is to let it go or give it up.

clue.text: Totally allow English to consent to making case

indicators.note: the outer word forms a case round the inner letters

parts.note: to consent to something is to comply
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: Fully permit an Englishman to agree to build a legal argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Completely and totally both mean wholly, to the full extent.

clue.text: Get better men with merit to secure European trophy

indicators.note: the two outer words hold the inner ones fast between them

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is the crossword's usual source for 'men'
to merit something is to rate it
a cup is a sporting trophy

explanation.surface: A team improves by fielding deserving players so it can win a continental cup.
explanation.definitionFit: To recuperate is to recover from illness, that is to improve in health.

clue.text: Bob's never-ending choice

indicators.note: having no ending, the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a plumb bob is the weight on a plumb line, so bob gives the word plumb; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone called Bob keeps choosing without ever finishing.
explanation.definitionFit: A plum job is the choicest one, so as an adjective plum means excellent, top pick.

clue.text: Immediately prefer the other one after fair

indicators.note: the second part follows the first

parts.note: just means fair
preferring the other option is to say you like that one

explanation.surface: Someone at a fairground suddenly prefers a different ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like that' read as a verb phrase, 'I like that one', is the second half of an idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Just like that' is an idiom meaning suddenly, without delay or warning.

clue.text: Possibly handy passage in unstable nuclear plant

indicators.note: something unstable is liable to fall apart and re-form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A corridor that could be useful inside a dangerously unsafe nuclear power station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' warns that 'handy' is a pun: the passage is in the hand, at the wrist.
explanation.definitionFit: The carpal tunnel is a narrow passage through the wrist bones, so it belongs to the hand in an anatomical sense.

clue.text: Kitty left following depression over topless part

indicators.note: the letter for left comes after the depression
in a down clue, over means placed above what follows

parts.note: a col is a dip between mountain peaks

indicators.note: with no top, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a section is a part

explanation.surface: A sad mood sets in after a cat strips off its top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kitty' suggests a cat but means a pooled fund.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitty is a pool of money gathered from several people, a collection.

clue.text: Nationalists tire over disclaimers in report

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part sits above the second

parts.note: to flag is to tire

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word is spoken and its sound used

parts.note: waivers are disclaimers, giving up a right

explanation.surface: Patriots grow weary of the legal disclaimers in a document.
explanation.definitionFit: Flag-wavers are people who make a loud show of patriotism, so the word suits nationalists.

clue.text: Figure that's new posted in old e-journal

indicators.note: posted into something means put inside it, so one letter goes into the others

parts.note: a blog is an online journal

explanation.surface: A figure that has only just been published in a web diary.
explanation.definitionFit: An oblong is a rectangle, a geometrical figure that is longer than it is wide.

clue.text: Deliberately do away with retiring journalist caught in bar

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

indicators.note: one letter is placed in the other word

parts.note: a strut is a supporting bar
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A reporter heading home is arrested in a pub and someone is bumped off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a pub but is a structural strut.
explanation.definitionFit: To destruct is to destroy something on purpose, as with a rocket's self-destruct button.

clue.text: Principal male in diocese I don't know

indicators.note: these letters go inside the other word

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese
arch as a prefix or adjective means chief, principal

explanation.surface: The leading man in a bishop's district admits ignorance.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Search me' is an informal idiom used when you have no idea of the answer.

clue.text: Things passed on in revolutionary prison stories going round

indicators.note: the outer word surrounds the inner

parts.note: stories in the sense of fibs are lies

indicators.note: a revolution turns things over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a cage is a prison

explanation.surface: Tales told in a rebel jail that are handed down over the years.
explanation.definitionFit: Legacies are bequests, possessions left to heirs in a will.

clue.text: Motor fashioned from cube with odd bits of steel

parts.note: a die is a small cube used in games

indicators.note: the first, third and fifth letters, the odd-numbered ones, are picked out

explanation.surface: An engine made out of a block of steel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashioned from' is a link, not an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A diesel is an engine that ignites its fuel by compression, or a vehicle driven by one.

clue.text: Brief course in fashion with extremely useful content

indicators.note: content as a noun is what is held, so the picked letters go inside

parts.note: a mode is a fashion

indicators.note: the extremes of the word, its first and last letters, are taken

explanation.surface: A short fashion course with plenty of practical material in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A module is a short self-contained unit of study within a larger programme.

clue.text: Terribly OTT breach backing male or female gossips

indicators.note: done terribly, these letters end up in a disordered arrangement
backing means moving in reverse, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: sex is the category of male or female

explanation.surface: An over-the-top breach of confidence has men and women alike gossiping.
explanation.walkthrough: OTT is British shorthand for over the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Chatterboxes are people who talk incessantly, so the word fits gossips as nouns.

clue.text: Bond caught countryman

indicators.note: caught as in caught what someone said, so it is the sound that counts

parts.note: a tie is a bond

explanation.surface: James Bond has nabbed a man from the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' suggests 007 and 'countryman' a rustic; it means someone from Thailand.
explanation.definitionFit: A Thai is a native of Thailand, a man of that country.

clue.text: Shown round part of Nineveh that's flat

indicators.note: turned round, the letters are read backwards
the letters are a part of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A tourist is shown around some of the ancient city of Nineveh, which is level.
explanation.definitionFit: Even ground is level, with no bumps, so flat is a synonym.

clue.text: Himalayan region uncovered by mountain dweller

indicators.note: with its covers removed, the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: Tibet is the high region north of the Himalayas
X is 'by' as in multiplication, three by four

explanation.surface: A Himalayan area gets laid bare by some creature living in the peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibex is a wild goat of high mountain country, with long curved horns.

clue.text: Premier source of old crisis?

definitions.meaning: Nikita ... was Soviet premier from 1958 to 1964
the Cuban missile crisis of 1962 came from the Soviet leader's placing of missiles in Cuba

explanation.surface: Which head of government caused a crisis long ago?
explanation.definitionFit: Khrushchev led the USSR as premier and his Cuban missiles set off the 1962 standoff.

clue.text: Every second in international homes, aspiring chefs making food

indicators.note: the second letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: Wannabe cooks in homes around the world turn out dishes nonstop.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosh is informal British slang for food or a meal.

clue.text: Son occupying newly repainted flat

indicators.note: to occupy is to sit inside, so this letter goes within the others
made new, these letters are put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A young man has moved into an apartment that was just decorated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' is not the apartment; it means dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedestrian means dull and uninspired, just as a lifeless performance is flat.
